scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1"; Phase 3 "Depends on: V2"; Phase 4 "Depends on: V1, V3, V4; quota increase"
scores.rationale: Each phase names its dependency and gates it on a validation that must pass first, so substrate comes before upper layers.

scores.evidence: an allow-listed staff member asks a real question (e.g. "How do I reset my password?") in the production widget. The answer streams back, grounded in a real public article
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real production end-to-end slice across all tiers, with deploy, rollback and trace, before any features.

scores.evidence: Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed with reversibility class, default, assumption, validation and concrete flip conditions, and the unknowns are labeled.

scores.evidence: Tasks, smallest exposure first: 1. Retention deletion job and widget privacy notice go live. 2. Load test...
scores.rationale: Phase 1 does the widest-impact guards first (redaction, renderer, filters), Phase 2 fixes the schema first, and Phase 4 runs smallest exposure first.

scores.evidence: 0 | Staff allow-list + flag; secrets in a vault; text treated as data; token caps; provider spend limit
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security controls for every phase from 0 to 5.

scores.evidence: OpenTelemetry trace per turn has one span per tier. Each trace records the model ID, prompt version and index version.
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in each later phase.

scores.evidence: index_version = corpus snapshot + chunker + embedding model; rebuild-from-scratch script
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is covered in every phase: IaC and a pinned image, versioned suites, index versions, versioned prompts and eval sets, and cohort config snapshots.

scores.evidence: LLM timeout → static fallback; pipeline rollback
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in every phase, from the Phase 0 fault injection through the circuit breaker, blue/green alias, fallback model, kill switch and outage drill.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: Defenses and budgets ... Phase 2: Retrieval ... Phase 3: Model access, generation, session memory, orchestration
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human handoff come first, then retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration, routing (deferred) and feedback, in the correct order.

scores.evidence: Model routing / multiple models. Pulled forward if V5 fails on cost or volume grows past provider quotas.
scores.rationale: Each deferred item has an explicit pull-forward condition.

note: Very strong plan: it has a real production skeleton, gates with flip conditions, threaded cross-cutting concerns, and AI layers in the correct order. I found no significant weaknesses.
